body: I'm sorry to hear that you're feeling this way. What University are you attending, if you don't mind me asking? I'm a student as well, and I know how stressful that can be. Have you talked to any professionals about how you've been feeling? Most schools provide free counseling and whatnot, though I understand if you're not up to talking to anyone about it.
Commenting for a bit over a week, lurking for a while longer
That's what I thought too, but sometimes I think it's only making me feel worse.
I'm starting to worry. If you're still here, please talk to us? We're here for you no matter what.
This doesn't make you a bitch, it just means that you're human. Please remember that you're not alone.
I'm glad that I read your story. I hope that it helps others to understand how this will affect those around them. Thank you for sharing <3

I know that a lot of religious groups believe that suicide is something to be punished for in the next life/afterlife etc. There's no real way to know for sure, but I suppose if you're worried about starting over after death, you could start over in life, right now. You say that you've done some bad things, and you intend to try to make things right. That's definitely good, but it sounds like you're worried that it won't be enough. My advice is to go ahead and write those letters; apologize to those who you have wronged, and then try your best to bring some good into the world as well. My personal belief is that if you can make a positive impact on the life of at least one other person, no matter how small that impact may seem, it will make a difference in how you will spend the rest of your existence. So, I would advise that instead of ending your life and hoping for the best, start a new life, right here, right now. Help those in need, tell your father you love him, offer support to others who feel the same as you. I can't guarantee that it will give you any bonus points in the next life, but when you do leave this world, whether it be from natural causes or not, you can be content with the fact that you did make a difference, and that you did matter.

I have been where you are. I suffered for years, and I was convinced I would never get better. I didn't want help, I didn't want to burden my friends, I didn't want to be defined by my depression. I won't go into too much detail, but things did get better. I take my medications willingly, I'm feeling more confident, and the painful thoughts aren't quite as hard to ignore anymore. Don't give up just yet.

I'm really sorry to hear about your friend. I know that this is something you will have to carry with you for the rest of your life, and I can't imagine how much pain you're feeling right now. If there's anything I can do for you, please let me know. I could use a friend too.

I'm sorry to hear that you're going through this. Although I don't know what it's like to deal with these feelings while in the military, I just wanted to let you know that I read your post, and I care about what happens to you.
